title: Residency Assertions and Failover Quarantine for Private/VPC Deployments
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Goal: Implement a failover-safe residency enforcement layer for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that ensures (1) live requests never cross prohibited jurisdictions, (2) temporary failovers enter a quarantine mode that preserves residency guarantees, and (3) automated evidence bundles are produced for audits without exposing sensitive payloads.

Context: Customers with strict data residency requirements expect both steady-state guarantees (requests/processors pinned to region or on-prem) and predictable behavior during regional outages. Existing routing falls back to the nearest healthy region which can violate contractual residency constraints for Private deployments. We need a combinable policy + runtime approach that integrates with the control plane, serving runtime, and audit pipeline.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI for SSO-based admin controls (console work will follow), nor does it change hosted API pricing. It focuses on enforcement, evidence generation, and an operator-visible quarantine mode.

Requirements: 1) Residency Assertion Tokens (RATs): a compact signed statement attached to routing decisions that declares effective residency binding for a request. RATs must be verifiable by local proxies and included in evidence bundles.
2) Quarantine Mode: when a region fails or is unhealthy, for Private/VPC deployments we must support 3 quarantine behaviors selectable per customer: "hold" (queue incoming writes until region recovers), "local-process-only" (process only on pinned on-prem hosts), and "restricted-fallback" (failover only to pre-approved secondary DCs).
3) Audit Bundle Automation: when quarantine events occur, generate an immutable audit bundle that contains RATs, routing traces, decision reasons, timestamps, and anonymized token-level cost summaries. Bundles must be signed with a KMS key and stored to the customer's configured audit sink (S3/GCS or on-prem collector).
4) On-prem compatibility: for air-gapped installs, provide a local evidence collector binary that can produce the same signed bundles; when offline, it should produce a gap report and a signed manifest describing missing artifacts.
5) Acceptance criteria: end-to-end test demonstrating (a) pinned workload never routes to unauthorized region during simulated failure, (b) quarantine mode triggered and policy behavior observed, (c) audit bundle generated and downloadable, (d) security review sign-off and storage encryption verified.

Constraints & risks: - Latency: additional signature verification (RATs) should not add >2ms p99 to routing path. We'll use ECDSA compact signatures and local caching of verification keys.
- Complexity: multiple quarantine behaviors require clear operator UX and observability to avoid accidental data loss.
- Secrets: KMS integrations must not leak keys; on-prem collector will use customer-managed HSM where available.

Design decisions (provisional): - RAT format: JSON-LD compact with fields {subject, allowed_regions, ttl, decision_id} signed by control-plane signing key.
- Policy engine: control plane evaluates policy, emits RAT, runtime fetches RAT via fast metadata channel.
- Quarantine enforcement: runtime will implement a soft-state quarantine flag per deployment; routing returns explicit HTTP 409 or 503 responses for queued/held requests depending on policy.
- Evidence bundle: tar.gz of metadata only (no PII/payload). Include signed manifest, RATs, routing traces, and operator notes.

Testing plan: 1) Unit tests for RAT generation/verification. 2) Integration tests with local proxy simulating region failover. 3) Chaos test: kill primary region, assert quarantine behavior, collect audit bundle. 4) On-prem: run evidence collector in isolated network and verify signed manifest creation.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to internal Dedicated and one pilot customer account. Start with "restricted-fallback" behavior for pilot and iterate. Monitor error rates, audit bundle generation latency, and p99 routing latency.

Metrics to observe: rat_verification_latency_ms_p99, quarantine_mode_triggered_count, audit_bundle_generation_duration_ms, audit_bundle_upload_failures, routing_denied_due_to_residency_count.

Open questions: 1) exact RAT expiry semantics for long-running streaming sessions. Proposal: bind RATs to a session token with revalidation every 30 minutes. 2) operator tooling for re-queuing held requests vs explicit client retries.

Delivery artifacts: design doc (Confluence), runtime PR, control-plane PR, on-prem collector binary, E2E test harness, and a security review ticket.
